title: U.S. House · Ohio's 10th District
area: Southwest Ohio, including Dayton and Montgomery County.

context.text: Incumbent Michael Turner (R) advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Kristina Knickerbocker won the Democratic primary. Thomas McMasters won the Libertarian primary.

summary.text: Michael Turner is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 10th Congressional District, which he has represented since 2003. A Dayton native, he was a business and real estate attorney and served as mayor of Dayton before entering Congress, where he sits on the Armed Services and Oversight committees and chaired the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence from 2023 to 2025.

background.text: Born in Dayton, Ohio. According to his official biography, his father worked in manufacturing in Dayton and his mother taught elementary school in Huber Heights; he attended Dayton Public Schools and graduated from Belmont High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio Northern University (1982), a law degree from Case Western Reserve University (1985) and an MBA from the University of Dayton (1992); his official biography also lists a Doctorate in Liberal Studies from Georgetown University (2022).
Practiced law in Dayton for more than 17 years and, in 1991, opened his own practice specializing in real estate and corporate law, according to his official biography.

Served as mayor of Dayton from 1994 to 2002. His official biography says he created Rehabarama, a public-private housing rehabilitation partnership, and established a development fund that awarded more than $19 million in grants.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and took office in 2003.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (with its Strategic Forces and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) and the Oversight Committee in the 119th Congress. He was ranking member of the Intelligence Committee in 2021-2022.
Chaired the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence from 2023 to 2025, according to his official biography.

Appointed chairman of the U.S. Delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in 2011 and elected president of the Assembly in December 2014; he now serves as vice-chairman of its Defense and Security Committee. His official biography also credits him with advocating for Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, including funding for a new National Air and Space Intelligence Center.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the House Committee on Armed Services, including its Strategic Forces and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 118th Congress (2023-2024), after serving as its ranking member in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Kristina Knickerbocker is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 10th Congressional District. She is a family nurse practitioner who served in the U.S. Air Force and Air Force Reserve from 2015 to 2025, including at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, and has worked as a neuro-oncology nurse practitioner at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. According to her campaign materials and interview, she is running on health care costs, affordability and reducing corruption in politics.

background.text: According to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she grew up active in church and volunteering at local food pantries and worked multiple jobs to put herself through school before pursuing nursing.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Azusa Pacific University (2014), a military citation from the University of Southern California (2015) and a graduate degree from The Ohio State University (2022).

Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2015 to 2025. As a major and nurse in the 88th Air Base Wing at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base she led medical teams, and she later served in the Air Force Reserve with the 445th Aeromedical Staging Squadron.
Moved to the Miami Valley a little over a decade ago when stationed at Wright-Patterson, and lives in Yellow Springs, according to the Yellow Springs News (April 2026).
Works as a family nurse practitioner, including as a neuro-oncology nurse practitioner at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center.

Describes herself as a mother of two. In an April 2026 interview she said she had not been "steeped in politics" before running and was motivated by seeing patients struggle with insurance coverage and costs; she was one of six Democrats on the May 5, 2026 primary ballot.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will protect Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP and the Affordable Care Act and support a public option.
positions.quote: I’ll protect Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP, and the Affordable Care Act; support a public option to lower premiums and expand care

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will repeal harmful tariffs that raise prices.
positions.quote: repeal harmful tariffs that raise prices

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will invest in law enforcement and fire departments and fight for more resources for local first responders.
positions.quote: I’ll invest in law enforcement, fire departments, and prevention strategies that strengthen safety while building trust in our communities.

candidates.name: Thomas McMasters

summary.text: Thomas McMasters is the Libertarian Party nominee for Ohio's 10th Congressional District. He is a U.S. Air Force veteran who has worked as a senior consultant, and has sought this seat before, in the 2012 Democratic primary and the 2016 general election as an independent. In his Ballotpedia survey he names military spending and readiness and efficiency in the use of tax dollars as his main policy interests.

background.text: Graduated from Orchard Park High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the State University of New York, Buffalo (1989) and a graduate degree from The Citadel (1997).
Served in the U.S. Air Force; Ballotpedia's profile lists his service as 1989 to 2009, and in his Ballotpedia survey he says he entered military service in 1983 and retired from active duty in 2009.
Has worked as a senior consultant.
Ran for this seat in the 2012 Democratic primary, which Sharen Neuhardt won, and in 2016 as an independent, receiving 3.2% (10,890 votes) against incumbent Michael Turner.

priorities.text: Describes himself as anti-war while advocating for a strong military.
priorities.quote: I am anti-war while also advocating for a strong military.

priorities.text: Lists military spending and readiness, and efficiency and value for tax dollars, as the policy areas he is most passionate about.
priorities.quote: Military spending and readiness.  Efficiency and value for our tax dollars.

priorities.text: Supports removing party affiliation from the ballot.
priorities.quote: I believe that eliminating party affiliation on the ballot would be helpful.

statements.quote: We don't need ICE going to swearing in ceremonies to deport people that have legitimately made it that far into the citizenship process.

statements.quote: We aren't going to get rid of fossil fuel-based power, but we can't be antagonist to green energy either.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his own campaign website (answers to the League of Women Voters questions, 2026; one 2019 post). No stated position found that directly takes a side on the guide's issue statements, so only statements are shown. His tommcmasters.org site blocked automated access and was not used.
